records.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
records.reason: Full text confirms a direct inference-efficiency contribution: SBERT replaces repeated cross-encoder pairwise BERT inference with reusable sentence embeddings and cosine similarity, reducing the paper's 10,000-sentence clustering example from about 65 hours to 5 seconds. However, the method is for sentence similarity/search with BERT encoders, not LLM generation or a serving system, and its scope does not establish whether this task-level retrieval optimization counts as an LLM inference-efficiency technique. Retain as borderline for root scope review.
records.body_check: Full primary PDF reviewed, focusing on §§1, 3–7 and conclusion. Method: fine-tune BERT/RoBERTa in siamese or triplet form with pooling to produce fixed-size sentence embeddings; similarity at inference uses cosine distance, permitting one embedding per sentence rather than a cross-encoder call for every pair. Evaluation: STS and transfer benchmarks assess embedding quality; §7 compares throughput on an Intel i7-5820K and Nvidia V100. Table 7 reports SBERT-base 44 CPU / 1378 GPU sentences/s and smart-batched SBERT 83 / 2042; smart batching is 89% faster on CPU and 48% on GPU than unbatched SBERT, and GPU throughput is about 9% above InferSent and 55% above Universal Sentence Encoder. The conclusion gives the 10,000-sentence example (about 50 million pair computations / 65 hours with BERT versus 10,000 embeddings / about 5 seconds with SBERT). Limits relevant to scope: CPU SBERT is about 65% slower than InferSent; GPU result is a specific V100 sentence-embedding benchmark; cross-topic argument similarity drops by about 7 Spearman points versus in-topic evaluation; the paper does not evaluate generative LLM serving. ACL Anthology metadata confirms DOI and title; packet source URL resolves to the matching arXiv preprint.

records.title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Sentence Classification
records.reason: The primary abstract describes experiments using a one-layer CNN over pretrained word vectors for sentence-level classification and reports task-accuracy gains. It does not present an LLM inference/serving system or an inference-efficiency technique; being a general NLP neural model is insufficient for this scope.
records.body_check: Primary ACL Anthology metadata and PDF abstract checked. The abstract identifies the method as CNN sentence classification with pretrained/static and fine-tuned word vectors, evaluated on classification benchmarks including sentiment and question classification. This is clearly outside scope from the abstract; full text was not required.

records.title: Deep Contextualized Word Representations
records.reason: The primary abstract describes ELMo contextual word representations learned from internal states of a pretrained bidirectional language model and downstream NLP accuracy improvements. It does not describe a serving system or an inference-time efficiency/compression contribution; the use of a language model as a representation source alone is insufficient for this scope.
records.body_check: Primary ACL Anthology metadata and abstract checked. The abstract states that ELMo representations are functions of a pretrained biLM's internal states, added to task models to improve six NLP tasks; the contribution is representation quality and task performance, not LLM inference/serving efficiency. This is clearly outside scope from the abstract; full text was not required.
